highlights: SCAP ordered 292 Japanese Army and Navy hospitals with 156,725 beds transferred to the Ministry of Health and Welfare for civilian use, against existing civilian capacity of 142,926 beds.
By 30 December 1945, 924,584 Japanese nationals had returned to Japan, while 654,523 Koreans, Chinese, Formosans and Ryukyuans were repatriated from the Home Islands.
The 1 November 1945 census put Japan's population at 71,996,477, with major cities such as Tokyo falling by up to 60 percent because of wartime dispersal.
A Tokyo nutrition survey examined 33,000 residents and 2,777 households and, with post-mortem findings, found no evidence for rumors of widespread civilian starvation deaths.
Emergency DDT dusting, an airlift of DDT and quarantine procedures cut weekly typhus cases among Hokkaido coal miners from 151 in early November to 44 in December.
SCAP intervened in the Japanese Cabinet's civil service retrenchment plans to prevent indiscriminate 50 percent personnel cuts among technical public health staff.
The Japanese government was directed to administer destitution relief and distribute military reserve stocks, while SCAP issued a new venereal disease control ordinance.
A national refresher course trained 250 public health nurses from 46 prefectures, and the Nurses Association petitioned for self-governing status.

summary: This December 1945 monthly report details early U.S. Occupation efforts to stabilize public health, welfare, and sanitation across Japan amidst severe post-surrender dislocation. Major developments include the containment of typhus outbreaks in Hokkaido using DDT dusting, the introduction of quarantine protocols at repatriation ports, and the directed transfer of 292 Imperial Army and Navy hospitals to the Ministry of Health and Welfare to nearly double civilian bed capacity. SCAP established civilian relief responsibilities, initiated comprehensive urban nutrition surveys in Tokyo to evaluate starvation rumors, and distributed surrendered military medical reserves while combating severe shortages of penicillin, vaccines, and raw materials. Legally, SCAP enacted venereal disease control measures, protected technical health personnel from indiscriminate government layoffs, and received petitions for self-governance from the national nurses’ association. For historians, the report provides invaluable baseline data on early postwar conditions, including the complete November 1945 population census showing extensive wartime urban-to-rural displacement, detailed livestock and disease statistics, repatriation volumes of Koreans and Japanese nationals, and the initial institutional rebuilding of Japan’s public welfare administration.
